newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mar natgas prices skid on weather, stocks-NGC.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mar natgas prices skid on weather, stocks-NGC.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices continued to fall sharply in March, again pressured by mild U.S. weather patterns and adequate storage levels, Natural Gas Clearinghouse (NGC) said Friday.
U.S. spot gas prices for March averaged $1.65 per million British thermal units, down $1.13 from February's average of $2.78. Last March, spot prices averaged $2.31, NGC said in its monthly survey.
The largest monthly losses were in Oklahoma, where prices on pipelines like Northern Natural in Beaver County slumped $1.25 for the month to $1.55, about 30 cents under last year.
Most Gulf pipes were off by about $1.10-1.15 for the month and were now about $1.10 below the same year-ago month.
Prices into Columbia Gas tumbled $1.10 from February to $1.75, about $1.10 below last year's levels, NGC said.
Sales into El Paso Natural Gas in west Texas averaged $1.60, down $1.05 for the month and 25 cents below last year.

Prices represent NGC estimates of the median price for one month spot transactions at the indicated receipt points. The estimates are based upon quotes by industial end-users and local distribution companies, NGC said.
